title: A phase's status is derived, so a finished phase stops holding the gate
description: F466, operator decision 2026-09-24: derived status with recorded sign-off; sign-off due does not hold the gate.
desiredOutcome: a phase whose tasks are all terminal and whose sign-off is recorded (and, with a branch, merged) reads done everywhere; one only awaiting sign-off reads 'sign-off due' and no longer holds the plan gate in deny; sign-off is recorded by a verb

tasks.title: The derived phase status, named once beside effective_bug_status
tasks.description: effective_phase_status, signoff_recorded, signoff_due and phase_running: the one answer every reader of a phase's status will ask.

outcome.descriptive: There is one answer to whether a phase is finished, running, or waiting for sign-off.

tasks.title: The plan gate reads phase_running, and area rules stay live through sign-off
tasks.description: manifest_state's phaseRunning comes from _manifest_io.phase_running, so a phase only awaiting sign-off no longer holds the denying tier (operator decision); it is named as signoffDuePhase. Area-scoped policy stays live while a phase is running OR sign-off due, because sign-off's fix runs work in that area; the hook and the panel preview ask one function.

outcome.technical: manifest_state via phase_running with signoffDuePhase; active_area_tags and the panel twin via area_active.
outcome.descriptive: A phase only awaiting sign-off no longer holds the plan gate in deny; area rules stay live through sign-off.

tasks.title: area_active, and the fixtures that described a running phase with no work left
tasks.description: The shared area rule P63.2's hook and panel call, and the fixtures that change meaning under it - committed apart from P63.2 because P63.2 did not declare them, and landed right after it because P63.2's commit calls area_active.

outcome.technical: _manifest_io.area_active; ds15/s10d fixtures carry an open task.
outcome.descriptive: The area rule and the fixtures that change meaning under it are committed.

tasks.title: audit-task signoff: sign-off recorded by a verb, the status derived from it
tasks.description: signoff <phaseId> --verdict passed|skipped --summary TEXT [--review-outcome TEXT]: refuses open tasks, a closed phase and a second sign-off; writes review.status, review.outcome and summary, clears the claim, journals phase.signoff, and never writes status - it is derived.

outcome.technical: audit-task signoff writes review.status/outcome and summary, clears the claim, journals phase.signoff; status stays derived.
outcome.descriptive: A phase is signed off by one command, and reads done from that record - on its parent branch too.

tasks.title: The status surfaces read the derived phase status
tasks.description: status_index (what a blockedBy on a phase resolves through) and the rollup's phase status are effective_phase_status; the rollup carries signoffDue; audit-status and the doctor's plan-gate line say which phases await sign-off. The CI in-progress condition is unchanged on purpose: a phase awaiting sign-off still reads in_progress.

outcome.technical: status_index and rollup via effective_phase_status; signoffDue in the rollup and on the status line; doctor gate line names its reason.
outcome.descriptive: Status, readiness and the doctor read a signed-off phase as done and say which phases await sign-off.

tasks.title: The report reads the derived status, releases 'held by' on any terminal blocker, and says sign-off due
tasks.description: The phase meta line's merge note reads the derived status (a phase signed off and merged is done, not 'sign-off not recorded'), a phase awaiting sign-off says so, 'held by' clears on a cancelled blocker as it does everywhere else, and the Markdown twin names sign-off due.

outcome.technical: meta line via effective_phase_status and signoff_due; _settled_ids over TERMINAL; md heading flag.
outcome.descriptive: The shareable report shows a signed-off phase as done, names a phase awaiting sign-off, and stops showing a cancelled blocker as holding work.

tasks.title: Cleanup after a merge reads the derived status, so a phase signed off by the verb is settled
tasks.description: phase_settled demanded a stored status done, which the signoff verb never writes - so close-phase would merge a signed-off phase and then refuse to remove its worktree and branch. The status comes in as status_of, the way terminal already does, and every caller passes effective_phase_status.

outcome.technical: met - phase_settled takes status_of; close-phase, manage-worktrees and both panel paths pass effective_phase_status; q1s/q1u/k4s/k4u/q1c, each seen red under its mutation
outcome.descriptive: Removing a merged phase's worktree and branch, and the cleanup the panel offers, now work for a phase signed off with the signoff command, instead of refusing it as unfinished.

tasks.title: Every remaining reader of a phase's status asks the derived one
tasks.description: The priority skip note, the pin warning, the mid-run migration refusal, the ADO link state, usage economics, doctor's parent-branch check and stale-merge note, the status command's running phase and blocked-by line, the journal's phase.signoff derivation, and audit-task's phase resolution, labels and refusals all read the stored status. Each asks the derived one; a signed-off phase is refused new tasks and retargeting the way a done one is; the verb's own journal row is phase.verdict so the hook's derived phase.signoff is not written twice.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__usage_economics.py: budget row carries the derived status
plugins/audit/tests/test_migrate_manifest.py: sign-off due with and without a branch

outcome.technical: met - every stored-status reader moved to effective_phase_status / phase_running; rollup carries running; journal derives phase.signoff from the derived status and the verb writes phase.verdict; each fix seen red under its reversal
outcome.descriptive: The status command, doctor, the ADO link state, priority notes, migration, the journal and the task verbs now agree that a signed-off phase is done and that a phase only awaiting sign-off is not a running one.
